claim: No Pi tool surface can cancel or shut down a detached invocation: both registered producers launch with permissions [inspect,execute] so the host denies cancel/shutdown at the socket, and workflow_control's local-detached leg is doubly dead because the W13-G reader that would seed confirmed ownership (applyDetachedReading) is never wired in production — control.ts:36 and docs/workbench/11:14 still advertise local-detached cancel/shutdown. Only recourse: read pid from the receipt and signal by hand, or wait out timeoutMs (default 24h).
evidence: Probe: node probes/detached/probe-main.mjs P2 — launch with permissions ['inspect','execute'] exactly as src/index.ts:2672 and :2925 hard-code, then client.cancel() -> 'Detached authorization: Invocation cancel grant denied.'; client.shutdown() -> 'Detached authorization: Invocation shutdown grant denied.'; process.kill(receipt.pid,'SIGTERM') then worked. Code chain: src/index.ts:2925 (workflow_detached) and :2672 (workflow_execute detached) both pass permissions:['inspect','execute']; src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:777 denies unpermitted verbs; src/workbench/control.ts:232-233 denies without confirmed ownership ('no confirmed lifecycle ownership'); grep -rln detached-observer src/ -> only src/workbench/detached-observer.ts itself (importers are tests only: test/workbench-detached-control-live.test.ts:217 seeds the projection manually).
cost: Any operator or agent with a runaway detached run (deterministic default timeout 24h): every stop requires out-of-band SIGTERM; the advertised workflow_control destructive actions for local-detached can never settle in a real session.
cureHint: Grant cancel+shutdown in the two producers (src/index.ts:2673,:2925) or expose permissions as a launch param, and call applyDetachedReading after launch/inspect so decideControl can confirm ownership.

claim: On any host whose $HOME contains a symlink (standard Amazon cloud-desktop layout /home/<user> -> /local/home/<user>), every workflow_detached launch and every workflow_execute hostMode:detached refuses with 'Authorization: unsafe detached directory ancestor.' because the launch directory join(getAgentDir(),'workbench-detached') inherits the symlinked home and ancestors() lstat-refuses symlink ancestors; the message names neither the offending ancestor nor any remediation (PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to a realpath works but is undocumented).
evidence: Probe P8: ls -ld /home/jehallad -> 'lrwxrwxrwx ... /home/jehallad -> /local/home/jehallad'; os.homedir() -> /home/jehallad; launchDetachedWorkflow({directory:'/home/jehallad/.pi/agent/workbench-detached',...}) threw 'Authorization: unsafe detached directory ancestor.' and wrote nothing. Code: src/index.ts:2918 directory=join(getAgentDir(),'workbench-detached'); src/agent-dir.ts:53 join(homedir(),'.pi','agent'); src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:186-194 ancestors() refuses stat.isSymbolicLink().
cost: 100% launch failure for the whole detached feature on symlinked-home fleets; the terse message gives no path to diagnosis, so operators conclude the feature is broken.
cureHint: realpathSync the agent dir (or the directory argument) before ancestors(), and have ancestors() name the failing ancestor and the PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR workaround in its message.

claim: A completed detached run's terminal verdict and result become permanently unrecoverable once retentionMs (default 10 min, max 1 h) expires: the host exits, unlinks its socket, and inspect thereafter returns observation unknown / terminal unknown with the crash-reconcile hint and no result; nothing in the invocation directory (invocation.json + receipt.json only) records that the run completed or what it returned. 'Survives Pi disconnect' holds only inside the retention window.
evidence: Probe P1: launch retentionMs:1500 -> terminal snapshot {observation:'observed-terminal',terminal:'completed',result:{ok:true,...}}; after sleep 2600ms the same client.inspect() -> {observation:'unknown',terminal:'unknown',resultPresent:false,diagnostic:'ENOENT ... .sock',reconcileHint:'Host connection lost: JavaScript state is not recoverable...'}. Design stance declared at src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:7-9 ('never a saved terminal verdict') and docs/workbench/08:67-69; retention bounds at local-detached.ts:461 (100..3600000, default 600000).
cost: Anyone who reattaches more than retentionMs after completion (Pi restart, lunch, overnight): the workflow's answer is gone and the state is indistinguishable from a crash, inviting needless reconciliation.
cureHint: Write an observation-grade terminal file (verdict + result digest + boundedresult) beside receipt.json at terminal time, clearly labeled as saved observation rather than live host truth.

claim: The typed snapshot cannot distinguish the three cold states — crashed host, gracefully retired host, and never-launched invocation id: all return observation 'unknown', terminal 'unknown' and the identical 'Host connection lost: JavaScript state is not recoverable...' reconcile hint; the only discriminator is the raw OS errno string inside diagnostic (ECONNREFUSED vs ENOENT lstat socket vs ENOENT lstat invocation-dir). For a never-launched id the 'connection lost / reconcile known native effects' guidance is outright misleading: no host ever existed.
evidence: Probe P1 afterRetention diagnostic 'ENOENT ... pw-27639525/d8d1316743be5026.sock'; probe P3 afterCrash diagnostic 'connect ECONNREFUSED ... 1b02c56012eda178.sock' with socketLeftBehind:true; probe P4 never-launched diagnostic "ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '.../hosts/never-launched'" with the same reconcileHint; typed-field comparison crashVsRetirementDistinguishable:false. Code: src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:613-620 collapses every transport error into the one unknown snapshot with RECONCILE (:53).
cost: Agents must regex OS errno strings to triage; a typo'd invocationId reads as a lost host with effect-reconciliation duties, so agents park healthy work for phantom reconciliation.
cureHint: Add a typed cause field (no-such-invocation | socket-missing | connection-refused | transport-timeout) derived from errno plus invocation-directory existence, and drop the reconcile hint for no-such-invocation.

claim: A detached workflow that COMPLETES with a value larger than the 256 KiB snapshot bound is reported terminal:'failed' with no result: the terminal classifier overwrites the true completed status when safeJson refuses the oversized value, so a successful run (whose native effects all happened) presents as a failure.
evidence: Probe P5: script 'return "x".repeat(300*1024)' -> snapshot {terminal:'failed',diagnostic:'Workflow returned a result exceeding the bounded JSON snapshot contract.',resultPresent:false}. Code: src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:741-743 — terminal set to 'completed' then reassigned 'failed' in the safeJson catch.
cost: Agents and operators mis-triage successful runs as failures and may re-run or reconcile work that already succeeded; any workflow returning large payloads hits it every time.
cureHint: Keep terminal:'completed' and add resultOmitted:'exceeds-snapshot-bound' (result stays absent) instead of reclassifying the run as failed.

claim: Detached launches from both registered tools hard-code providers:[], so a detached script can never call any native capability (forge.gate.status, hyperunix.find, reactivefiber.render.preview, furnace.run.inspect) even when the operator holds the exact grants — the same script works in embedded mode where registerNativeProviders wires all four. Detached mode silently loses the README's flagship node('forge.gate.status') capability with only a generic capability error at run time.
evidence: src/index.ts:2925 (workflow_detached launch: providers:[]) and src/index.ts:2672 (workflow_execute detached launch: providers:[]); src/workbench/native-modules.ts:95-100 registerNativeProviders registers all four for the embedded registry; src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:464-476 registryFor builds the child registry only from request.providers. README.md:4 promises node('forge.gate.status') for workbench scripts without stating the embedded-only limit.
cost: Script authors who move a working embedded workflow to the detached host lose every native observation; the failure appears only mid-run as a capability refusal, not at launch preflight.
cureHint: Derive providers from held grants at both launch sites (mirror the embedded registry's grant-driven set) or refuse at launch when the script's node() targets are unreachable.

claim: workflow_detached launch cannot parameterize the run at all: input is hard-coded null (scripts observe args===null) and timeoutMs, retentionMs, permissions and providers are not exposed as tool params (schema: action, invocationId, scriptPath, trustedScript, backend only); the only input-carrying detached path is workflow_execute, which demands a digest-pinned saved definitionRef.
evidence: src/index.ts:2915 tool parameters Type.Object({action,invocationId,scriptPath,trustedScript,backend}); src/index.ts:2923-2925 launch object 'input:null, ... permissions:["inspect","execute"]'; workflow_execute carries launch.input at src/index.ts:2671 but requires definitionRef{id,schemaVersion,artifactDigest} (src/workbench/execute-tool.ts:176+).
cost: Agents on the quick path discover at run time that their arguments vanished; every parameterized detached run must first be saved and digest-pinned through the execute path.
cureHint: Add optional input (JSON), timeoutMs and retentionMs to workflow_detached's launch parameters and pass them through.

claim: A detached child that fails during startup dies silently: the compiled entrypoint catches every startup error and exits 1 with no diagnostic, production spawns with stdio:'ignore', and no failure record is written to the invocation directory; the launcher then reports only 'Detached host exited before handshake; invocation reserved, do not retry automatically.' — with the invocation id burned and nothing to diagnose from.
evidence: Probe P7: node dist/workbench/hosts/local-detached.js --serve /nonexistent-boot-pin.json sha256:000... -> status 1, stdout '' (stderr carries only Node's MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning, which stdio:'ignore' would hide). Code: src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:806 '.catch(() => { process.exit(1); })'; spawn stdio:'ignore' at :549; launcher text at :554.
cost: Any environment-shaped startup failure (bad runtime closure, changed pins, fs races) costs an opaque burned id per attempt; triage requires strace or editing dist by hand.
cureHint: In the entrypoint catch, write a redacted error.json beside the boot pin before exit and have the launcher's pre-handshake error name that file.

claim: Refusal and receipt craftsmanship worth protecting: the invocation-ID-conflict message names the reserved directory, states the never-reuse rule and the exact next step; the socket-path-bound refusal reports the measured byte count, the base source and two concrete remediations; execute-tool's missing-detach-grant names both required grant tokens; and the launch receipt is a compact (1174-byte) typed JSON that honestly declares security 'same-machine-os-dac-only', lifetime 'survives-client-disconnect-not-host-crash' and nativeRuntimeIdentity 'unsupported'.
evidence: Probe P1/P3 relaunch: 'Detached invocation ID conflict: p1-quick is already reserved by an earlier launch (...p1-quick exists); IDs are never reused, even after a dead host, so a deliberate second execution needs a NEW invocation ID.'; probe P6: 'Detached Unix socket path exceeds the 103-byte Linux socket path bound (104 bytes) under tmpdir base /xxx...; set XDG_RUNTIME_DIR to a short private directory (owner-only, mode 0700) or use a shorter TMPDIR.'; src/workbench/execute-tool.ts:216 'detached hostMode requires both workbench:execute and workbench:detach; execute alone never reaches a detached launch'; probe P1 receiptJsonBytes:1174 with the three honesty fields.

claim: The core detached lifecycle machinery works end-to-end in this environment: launch handshake 1342 ms cold; reattach-inspect from a fresh process returns the live receipt; completion delivers the result; cancel/shutdown settle correctly on fully-permissioned hosts; a crashed host's reserved id can never be rebound; the shipped QA journey passes and the three targeted vitest suites pass 120/120.
evidence: Probe P1 handshakeMs:1342, terminal 'completed' with result; probe P2 sigterm fallback stopped the host; bash qa/workbench/local-detached.sh -> exit 0 ('L1 detached: actual setsid process survives parent exit, reattach same UID, ... owned cancel, observer denial, unknown after loss, injection denied'); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-local-detached.test.ts test/workbench-detached-grants.test.ts test/workbench-detached-socket-base.test.ts -> 'Test Files 3 passed (3) / Tests 120 passed (120)'. hx census: hx --workspace $PIN exports src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts --best-effort -> 24 exported bindings; hx children test --best-effort | grep -c 'test/workbench-detached' -> 12 direct detached test files (plus local-detached/pi-detached suites).

claim: wb-71q class, measured: with no private runtime base (no XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, no /run/user/<uid>), any TMPDIR longer than 62 bytes (uid 27639525; threshold shrinks with longer uids) refuses every detached launch against the 103-byte sun_path bound; feature-matrix.md:172 states the defect as 'TMPDIR exceeds ~34 bytes', which misstates the measured envelope by nearly 2x.
evidence: Probe P6 sweep over resolveDetachedSocket({env:{},runUserRoot:'/nonexistent',tmpdir:'/x'*N}): maxTmpdirBytesThatLaunch 62, first refusal at 63 bytes: 'Detached Unix socket path exceeds the 103-byte Linux socket path bound (104 bytes) under tmpdir base ...'. Formula from src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:221-232: tmpdir + '/pw-<uid>-XXXXXX/' + 16hex + '.sock'. Matrix text: docs/workbench/feature-matrix.md:172 '~34 bytes'.
cost: Containers/CI with long TMPDIR and no per-user runtime dir cannot launch at all; the stale ~34-byte figure misleads anyone sizing a workaround.
cureHint: Shorten the per-launch template (pw-<uid>- to p-) or hash the uid into the digest, and correct the matrix row to the formula (103 - len(tmpdir) - uid-dependent overhead).

claim: package.json lacks "type":"module", so every detached child start (and every QA runner invocation) re-parses dist/workbench/hosts/local-detached.js — Node prints MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON 'This incurs a performance overhead' on each launch; production hides the warning behind stdio:'ignore' but still pays the double parse on the latency-sensitive handshake path.
evidence: Probe P7 stderr and qa/workbench/local-detached.sh output both print: 'Warning: Module type of file://.../dist/workbench/hosts/local-detached.js is not specified ... Reparsing as ES module ... To eliminate this warning, add "type": "module" to .../package.json.'
cost: Every detached launch and QA run pays the reparse; stderr noise pollutes every qa/workbench runner log.
cureHint: Add "type":"module" to package.json (or emit the host entrypoint as .mjs).

claim: Agent discoverability fails the installed-docs test: the tool name workflow_detached appears nowhere in README.md or AGENTS.md and nowhere in docs/ outside the feature-matrix security row and historical receipts; the grant tokens (workbench:detach / workbench:observe), the receipt directory location (<agentDir>/workbench-detached), the never-reuse id rule and the trustedScript review assertion are documented only in source. An agent with README/AGENTS/skills alone cannot learn the launch parameters or where receipts live; the runtime tool description (2 sentences) is the entire public contract.
evidence: grep -rn workflow_detached README.md AGENTS.md docs/ -> only docs/workbench/feature-matrix.md:183 (security row) and docs/workbench/receipts/wb-wupg.md; grep -n -i detach README.md -> only Agent-tool background-mode prose (lines 28,195,633,731,804); README.md:4 is the sole workbench paragraph and names no tool. Tool description at src/index.ts:2914.
cost: Every agent/operator adopting the detached host must read src to drive it; wrong guesses burn non-reusable invocation ids.
cureHint: Add a README 'Workbench tools' section with one entry per tool: params, required grants, receipt directory, reattach and stop recipes.

claim: workflow_detached's permission refusal is one static string for both actions — 'Permission denied: explicit detached launch or observe grant required.' — naming neither the exact token the failed action needs (workbench:detach vs workbench:observe) nor the settings key (workbench.capabilityGrants), in contrast to execute-tool's refusal which names both tokens.
evidence: src/index.ts:2917 one message for both actions; contrast src/workbench/execute-tool.ts:216 'detached hostMode requires both workbench:execute and workbench:detach'. Grant vocabulary lives only in settings source (src/settings.ts:12-27).
cost: Agents guess grant spellings and settings keys; each wrong guess is a failed tool call.
cureHint: Per-action refusal: name the missing token and the workbench.capabilityGrants settings key.

claim: Liveness budgets are fixed and unobservable: 5 s launch handshake (100 x 50 ms poll), 3 s socket transport timeout on both ends, and a 60 s pre-start idle self-stop; none is configurable or recorded. Measured cold handshake was 1342 ms on an idle host, so a loaded host or cold cache can plausibly exceed the 5 s budget — and that failure burns the invocation id with 'effects unknown' although nothing ran; an autoStart:false host that idles out leaves no trace distinguishing idle-expiry from a crash.
evidence: src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:549-568 (handshake loop, 100 attempts x 50 ms, timeout text 'invocation reserved and effects unknown'), :594 and :765 (3000 ms socket timeouts), :799 idle interval (60000 ms vs lastObservation) with stop() leaving no record; measured handshakeMs 1342 (probe P1).
cost: Flaky launches on loaded hosts burn ids; slow-polling observers lose autoStart:false hosts to silent idle expiry.
cureHint: Accept bounded handshakeMs/idleMs launch params and append an idle-expiry/timeout row to controlAudit (or a terminal file) before stop().

claim: There is no way to enumerate detached invocations from any tool: workflow_detached has only launch|inspect, so after session loss an agent must recall invocation ids from its own transcript even though every receipt sits on disk under <agentDir>/workbench-detached/<id>/receipt.json.
evidence: src/index.ts:2915 action union is exactly launch|inspect; receipt layout from src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:195-200 paths() (invocation.json/receipt.json per id); no other tool reads that directory (grep workbench-detached src/ -> only the two launch sites and the control connect at src/index.ts:3048).
cost: Reattach after a lost session degrades to guessing ids or shelling into the agent dir by hand.
cureHint: Add action:'list' that reads the invocation directory and reports id, launchedAt, pid and socket-liveness per row.

claim: nativeRuntimeIdentity is a hard-coded 'unsupported' literal in every receipt and snapshot while the landed executable-identity module (src/workbench/executable-identity.ts, 347 lines) is imported by nothing in src/ — the identity observation capability exists but was never wired into the detached host, leaving a descriptor-only field that can never carry information.
evidence: src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:104 and :118 literal 'unsupported'; probe P1 receipt nativeRuntimeIdentity:'unsupported'; grep -rn executable-identity src/ --include=*.ts excluding the module itself -> no importers; docs/workbench/feature-matrix.md:173 caveat: 'wiring into the detached host (which previously hard-coded nativeRuntimeIdentity ...) ... remain W18 owner items'.
cost: Consumers of receipts carry a dead field; the W18 identity groundwork delivers no value in any real receipt.
cureHint: Wire the executable-identity observation into receipt construction for absolute-path runtimes, or drop the field from the receipt contract until W18 lands.
